chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Talbeena (a porridge made from barley flour) clears the sorrowful heart, just as the fingers clear sweat from the forehead.

key_terms.التَّلْبِينَة: A porridge or gruel made from barley flour, often cooked with honey or milk, known for its soothing properties.
key_terms.يَجْلُو: To wipe away, clear, or remove (impurities or sweat).

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and emotional benefit of eating Talbeena according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual and psychological benefits of Talbeena, a barley-based porridge, by comparing its soothing effect on a grieving heart to the physical relief of wiping sweat from the forehead. This metaphor underscores the tangible comfort it provides, reflecting the Shia tradition of linking dietary practices with emotional and spiritual well-being. The comparison emphasizes not just the removal of sorrow, but the gentle, cleansing nature of this sustenance in restoring inner peace.
